findings.observed_f1: With no prior equalities, f(1)=0 unfolds to f(1-1)=0, then 0=0. CLI reports object_definition; native proof tree confirms both induction unfolds.
findings.observed_budget: With f(0)=0 and f(1)=0 stored, f(2)=0 fails at local budget 3 and succeeds at local budget 4 in the unchanged committed implementation.
findings.source_trace: Equality deep entry consumes one round. f(2) at 3 unfolds to f(2-1) at 2, then f((2-1)-1) at 1. Its next object-definition attempt receives 0, and case-guard verification receives that same 0; the numeric base guard cannot be checked. A separate round-zero full guard check reports WD failure, and the equality search also gates Calculation at zero.
findings.reuse: MatchingOneArgByOne uses known_only_no_wd with round 0. It cannot generate Calculation evidence for 2-1=1. Adding that equality stores the bridge; the native successful proof cites f(2-1)=f(1) via argument matching and stored equality, then the existing f(1)=0.
findings.checked_short_control: After the original f(0)=0 and f(1)=0 assertions, adding only 2-1=1 makes f(2)=0 pass. Storing f(2-1)=0 or f(2-1)=f(1) also makes it pass.
findings.classification: kernel_problem: bounded recursive unfolding/case checking plus inability of known-only argument matching to compute an unstored numeric equality.
findings.fix_status: Diagnosis complete; K003 remains open, no kernel fix implemented.
